PyAEDT: hfss.post.reports_by_category.antenna_parameters("PeakRealizedGain", hfss.nominal_adaptive, infinite_sphere="3D").create()
hfss.post.get_solution_data(["PeakRealizedGain", "RadiationEfficiency", "RadiatedPower"], hfss.nominal_adaptive, report_category="Antenna Parameters", context="3D")

parameters.name: PeakGain / PeakDirectivity / PeakRealizedGain
parameters.description: Maxima over the sphere; realized gain includes mismatch loss (uses accepted vs incident power).

parameters.name: IncidentPower / AcceptedPower / RadiatedPower
parameters.description: Source power, power entering the structure (1-|Gamma|^2 weighted) and power crossing the radiation surface.

parameters.name: RadiationEfficiency / TotalEfficiency
parameters.description: Radiated/Accepted and Radiated/Incident.

parameters.name: FrontToBackRatio / BeamArea / MaxU / DecayFactor
parameters.description: Pattern shape metrics; decay factor relates to the sphere's field decay check.

tools.example:
hfss.insert_infinite_sphere(name="3D", x_step=1, y_step=1)
hfss.analyze()
hfss.edit_sources({"P1:1": ("1W", "0deg")})
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data(["PeakRealizedGain", "RadiationEfficiency", "TotalEfficiency", "FrontToBackRatio"],
                                   hfss.nominal_adaptive, report_category="Antenna Parameters", context="3D",
                                   variations={"Freq": ["2.45GHz"]})
for q in data.expressions:
    print(q, data.get_expression_data(q)[1])
tools.notes: Antenna parameters depend on the radiated-power calculation method (Design Settings) and on saved radiated fields for sweep frequencies (SaveRadFields). Native: CreateReport with "Antenna Parameters" report type and ["Context:=", "3D"].

tools.name: report category: Far Fields quantities (GainTotal/Theta/Phi/LHCP/RHCP/X/Y/L3X/L3Y, RealizedGain*, DirTotal*, rETotal/rETheta/rEPhi, AxialRatioValue, Polarization ratios, RCSTotal/Theta/Phi, NormalizedDirectivity)
tools.description: The angular quantities of the Far Fields category on an infinite sphere: gain, realized gain and directivity in total and per polarisation component (theta/phi, LHCP/RHCP circular, X/Y Ludwig-2, L3X/L3Y Ludwig-3 co/cross, slant when the sphere polarisation is Slant), radiated field magnitudes rE (V), axial ratio, polarisation ratios, RCS quantities for plane-wave excitations, and normalised directivity. They plot versus Theta/Phi (cuts, 3D polar), versus frequency at fixed angles, or versus incident-wave angles for RCS.
tools.usage:
Results > Create Far Fields Report > Rectangular / Radiation Pattern / 3D Polar Plot > Category: Gain | Realized Gain | Directivity | rE | Axial Ratio | Polarization Ratio | RCS ...
Expressions: dB(GainTotal), dB(RealizedGainLHCP), dB(DirTotal), mag(rETotal), dB(AxialRatioValue), dB(RCSTotal), GainL3X, GainL3Y, NormalizedDirectivity?

parameters.name: Gain vs Realized Gain vs Directivity
parameters.description: Gain = directivity x radiation efficiency; realized gain also includes mismatch; directivity ignores losses.

parameters.name: Polarisation components
parameters.description: Theta/Phi spherical, LHCP/RHCP circular, X/Y (Ludwig-2) and L3X/L3Y (Ludwig-3 co/cross-pol).

parameters.name: rE quantities
parameters.description: Radiated electric field scaled by distance (V), useful for absolute field levels and EMC.

parameters.name: RCS quantities
parameters.description: RCSTotal/RCSTheta/RCSPhi (m^2, dB gives dBsm) for scattering problems.

parameters.name: Sweeps
parameters.description: Theta, Phi, Freq, IWaveTheta/IWavePhi (incident angles), and design variables as families.

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.far_field(["dB(RealizedGainL3X)", "dB(RealizedGainL3Y)"], hfss.nominal_adaptive, sphere_name="3D")
rep.variations = {"Freq": ["10GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["0deg", "90deg"]}
rep.primary_sweep = "Theta"
rep.report_type = "Radiation Pattern"
rep.create("Co/cross-pol cuts")
ar = hfss.post.get_solution_data("dB(AxialRatioValue)", hfss.nominal_adaptive, report_category="Far Fields", context="3D",
                                 primary_sweep_variable="Theta", variations={"Freq": ["10GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["0deg"]})
tools.notes: Far-field quantities exist only for solutions with saved radiated fields (LastAdaptive always; sweeps need SaveRadFields). The sphere's coordinate system and polarisation setting determine theta=0 and the slant reference. The exact quantity list for the installed release comes from hfss.post.available_report_quantities("Far Fields", context="3D").

tools.name: Fields Calculator recipes: radiated power, Q factor, voltage/current/impedance from fields, SAR, loss in an object (Add > Fields library expressions)
tools.description: Standard calculator sequences that the Fields Calculator's Add > Fields library and PyAEDT's expression catalog encapsulate: radiated power (real Poynting normal-integrated over a surface), stored electric/magnetic energy and unloaded Q of an eigenmode (omega*W/P_loss), voltage along a line (E tangential integral), current around a loop (H tangential integral) and their ratio for a field-based impedance, SAR maxima, and ohmic/dielectric loss integrated over an object. Each becomes a named expression usable in plots, reports, output variables and Optimetrics goals.
tools.usage:
Fields Calculator (Results > Fields > Calculator): Add... > library of expressions; or build on the stack: Quantity > operations > Geometry > Integrate > Add... (name)
PyAEDT catalog keys (fields_calculator.add_expression): e.g. "voltage_line", "current_line", "radiated_power"? - list them with fields_calculator.expression_names / the expression_catalog.toml
Stack recipes:
  Prad:  Poynting > Real > Surface(Region) > Normal > Integrate
  We:    E > ComplexMag > Pow 2 > * eps0/4 (scalar) > Volume(Cavity) > Integrate
  Ploss: Ohmic_Loss > Volume(Conductor) > Integrate  (or Surface loss density on a surface)
  Q:     2*pi*f*(We+Wm)/Ploss (as an output variable combining named expressions)
  V:     E > Real > Tangent > Dot > Line(L) > LineValue > Integrate
  I:     H > Real > Tangent > Dot > Line(Loop) > LineValue > Integrate
  SAR:   Average_SAR > Volume(Tissue) > Maximum

parameters.name: Named expressions
parameters.description: Saved with the design, plottable as field overlays (scalar fields) or reported in the Fields category (integrated values).

parameters.name: Geometry entries
parameters.description: Objects, face lists, polylines and points drawn in the modeler; sheets inside the volume for power flow cuts.

parameters.name: Intrinsics
parameters.description: Frequency and phase (or time) at which the expression is evaluated; complex magnitudes are phase-independent.

tools.example:
ofr = hfss.post.ofieldsreporter
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
ofr.EnterQty("Poynting"); ofr.CalcOp("Real"); ofr.EnterSurf("Region"); ofr.CalcOp("Normal"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("Prad", "Fields")
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
ofr.EnterQty("Ohmic_Loss"); ofr.EnterVol("Coil"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("Pcoil", "Fields")
hfss.post.create_report(["Prad", "Pcoil"], hfss.nominal_sweep, report_category="Fields")
hfss.create_output_variable("eff", "Prad/(Prad+Pcoil)", solution=hfss.nominal_sweep)
tools.notes: Quantity names differ between solution types (Ohmic_Loss vs Volume_Loss_Density, Surface_Loss_Density); the calculator's Quantity list shows what the current design offers. Eigenmode designs report Q directly (Q(1)) without the calculator.
